units.source_text: 源氏合着和琴吟唱催马乐：“莎草生在贯川边，做个枕头软如绵。”

en.t: Genji sang a saibara song to the accompaniment of the wagon: "Sedge grows beside the Nukigawa; make it into a pillow, soft as cotton."

units.source_text: 声音温柔可爱。

en.t: His voice was gentle and charming.

units.source_text: 唱到“郎君失却父母欢”时，脸上现出微笑。

en.t: When he came to the line, "The young lord has lost his parents' delight," a smile appeared on his face.

units.source_text: 此时自然而然地奏出清弹，其音美不可言。

en.t: At that moment he naturally drew out a clear strain, and the beauty of the sound was beyond words.

units.source_text: 唱罢，对玉鬘说道：“来，你也弹一曲吧。

en.t: When he finished singing, he said to Tamakazura, "Come, you play a piece too."

units.source_text: 凡是技艺，须在人前不怕羞耻，方能进步。

en.t: In any art, one can improve only by not fearing embarrassment before others.

units.source_text: 只有《想夫怜》一曲，因为曲名未便明言，所以也有人把曲调记在心中，暗地里弹奏。

en.t: Only with the piece "Sofuren," because its title is awkward to say openly, do some people keep the melody in their hearts and play it in secret.

units.source_text: 至于其他乐曲，总须毫无顾虑，与任何人都合奏，才容易进步。”

en.t: As for other pieces, you should play together with anyone without hesitation; that is how you improve more easily."

units.source_text: 他恳切地劝告。

en.t: He urged her earnestly.

units.source_text: 玉鬘在筑紫时，曾请一个自称是京都某亲王家出身的老妇人教授和琴，她深恐教的有错误，所以不肯弹奏。

en.t: When Tamakazura was in Tsukushi, she had learned the wagon from an old woman who claimed to come from the household of a certain prince in Kyoto, but she deeply feared the teaching might be faulty, and so she refused to play.

units.source_text: 她希望源氏再弹下去，好让她学习，热心之极，不知不觉地将身子靠近他去，同时说道：“有什么风来帮助，使得琴音如此优美！”

en.t: She wanted Genji to keep playing so that she could learn, and in her eagerness she unconsciously leaned closer to him, saying, "What wind has come to help, making the sound of the koto so beautiful!"

units.source_text: 便倾耳而听。

en.t: Then she bent her ear and listened closely.

units.source_text: 映着篝火之光，那姿态异常艳丽。

en.t: In the glow of the bonfire, her figure was extraordinarily beautiful.

units.source_text: 源氏笑着说：“为了你这耳聪的人，才有沁人心肺的风吹来帮助呀。”

en.t: Genji smiled and said, "It is for someone with such keen ears as yours that a heart-piercing wind has blown in to help."

units.source_text: 说着，便把琴推向一旁。

en.t: As he spoke, he pushed the koto aside.

units.source_text: 玉鬘心甚讨厌。

en.t: Tamakazura found it deeply unpleasant.

units.source_text: 此时有众侍女在旁，源氏未便像以前一般调戏她，便掉转话头：“这些年轻人没有饱看抚子花，就回去了。

en.t: Since many ladies-in-waiting were nearby, Genji could not tease her as he had before, so he changed the subject: "Those young people went home without having their fill of the pinks."

units.source_text: 我总得请内大臣也来看看这个花园。

en.t: I really must invite the Minister of the Interior to come and see this garden as well.

units.source_text: 人世真是无常迅速啊！

en.t: How swiftly and uncertainly the world changes!

units.source_text: 约二十年前有一个雨夜，内大臣在谈话中提到你，竟像是眼前之事呢！”

en.t: On a rainy night about twenty years ago, the Minister of the Interior mentioned you in conversation, and it seems as though it happened right before my eyes!"

units.source_text: 便把当时情状约略告诉她。

en.t: Then he briefly told her what had happened at that time.

units.source_text: 感慨之余，即席吟诗：

en.t: Moved by his feelings, he composed a poem on the spot:
